interventions.speaker: EXPERT-COHORT
interventions.who: cohort criterion; what the labelled series did in this exact situation
interventions.body:
This patient's situation: prior positive biopsy. The panel alone does not answer, and that is the finding.

The criterion here is that the visible panel does not determine this decision: he already has a tissue diagnosis, so neither a high PI-RADS nor a rising PSA is new information. What decides it is the documented grade of the prior biopsy and the surveillance history, which live in the previous notes. Measured on the labelled series: none of the three panel
rules I carry for this situation (PSA >= 20, age >= 78, PI-RADS <= 2) applies to him, and among the
39 remaining labelled men in this situation no structured variable separates the two answers.

REGISTRAR: the previous notes are where this case is decided. Read them for the grade of the prior
biopsy (Gleason or ISUP), the number of biopsy sessions and their dates, and whether he is on a
surveillance protocol with a confirmatory biopsy due. Do not read this as 'defer' and do not read it
as 'biopsy'.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-LIBRARY
interventions.who: case library; the closest labelled precedents and what the reading urologist did with them
interventions.body:
The case library holds 49 labelled men in this same situation (Positive prior biopsy). The 3 closest by panel distance, and what the reading urologist did:
  1. distance 1.49: PI-RADS 4, PSA 6.5, PSAD 0.11, age 64, DRE Normal -> DEFER (uncertain). He wrote: "Need initial ISUP grade and MRI in men on active surveillance."
  2. distance 1.54: PI-RADS 4, PSA 6.8, PSAD 0.2, age 62, DRE Normal -> DEFER (borderline). He wrote: "All depends if the lesion has grown in size since 2024. If stable no biopsy , if increased in size I will do a biopsy."
  3. distance 1.58: PI-RADS 4, PSA 6.7, PSAD 0.2, age 67, DRE Normal -> BIOPSY (borderline). He wrote: "Active surveillance, only one previous biopsy 2 yrs ago. Stable findings (stable PIRADS4, slightly increasing PSA) -> borderline indication for biopsy. As only one previ…"

PRECEDENT: DEFER (weighted vote 0.32 for biopsy). Distance-weighted precedent is no better than chance here (0.47 leave-one-out): read the precedents for how this urologist reasons, not for the answer.

What the precedents are FOR: they show what this urologist looks at and how he phrases the call. What they are NOT: facts about this patient. Nobody may cite a precedent's grade, PSA or MRI as if it were his.

neighbours.free_text: Need initial ISUP grade and MRI in men on active surveillance.
All depends if the lesion has grown in size since 2024. If stable no biopsy , if increased in size I will do a biopsy.

Active surveillance, only one previous biopsy 2 yrs ago. Stable findings (stable PIRADS4, slightly increasing PSA) -> borderline indication for biopsy. As only one previous biopsy, would lean toward one confirmatory biopsy this time and potentially increase interval until next time. Alternative is to delay biopsy one year and do it then.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The EAU guidelines discuss the use of MRI-based indications for biopsy, particularly concerning the PI-RADS score and PSA density. "A PI-RADS threshold of $\\ge 3$ is used to trigger biopsy [135, 226, 264, 375], at the cost of missing a small number of mainly ISUP GG 2 cancers, especially in biopsy-naïve patients or in highly selected populations with high prevalence of csPCa (in which the MRI NPV decreases) [372, 472]." This requires establishing if the current clinical scenario meets the criteria for a biopsy based on the guideline.

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
Expert-Structured's suggestion of biopsy is not settled because the guideline requires assessing the patient against specific risk-adapted matrices involving PI-RADS and PSA density, which the panel variables alone do not fully capture. The precedent from the library shows that the decision hinges on the documented grade of the prior biopsy and surveillance history, which is a factor not explicitly addressed by the panel variables alone.

WHAT WE STILL NEED
The guideline requires assessing the patient against risk-adapted matrices involving PI-RADS and PSA density.
Prior biopsy status: Positive.
PI-RADS score: 4.
PSA density: 0.217 ng/mL².
The documented grade of the prior biopsy and the number and dates of biopsy sessions in the notes.
Whether the patient is on a surveillance protocol with a confirmatory biopsy due.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (clear). Last value 19.00 ng/mL over 3 points spanning 28 months; velocity +4.89 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 21 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 66.5 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 19.1-231.7.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report — the laboratory panel was not opened, so that block is imputed and my band is wider for it; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.64
  uncertainty  +/- 0.08 epistemic (95% band 0.47-0.80), of which 0.01 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  MODERATE ('supports' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 56% of the time over the 25 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the
surveillance history: those are in the notes, and the registrar has to carry them.

  EXPERT-FUSION      BIOPSY, p(biopsy)=0.64  ('supports' tier, fusion_nolab)

interventions.speaker: VERIFIER
interventions.who: second EAU reader; checks against the guideline whether this can be decided yet
interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents opened—radiology_report, psa_trend, and previous_notes—directly address the moderator's questions by providing information on the prior biopsy grade, the number/dates of biopsies, and surveillance status.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The panel protocol concluded with a weighted vote for BIOPSY (p=0.59), which aligns with the findings retrieved, specifically the registrar's report stating the prior biopsy confirmed ISUP group 2 malignancy.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. What is the documented grade (Gleason or ISUP) of the prior biopsy? Answered by the registrar: The prior biopsy confirmed ISUP group 2 malignancy.
Q2. What is the number and dates of prior biopsy sessions, and is the patient on a surveillance protocol with a confirmatory biopsy due? Answered by the registrar: There was one prior biopsy session recorded in December 2023, and the patient was engaged for further clinical evaluation.

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The documented prior biopsy grade (ISUP group 2) is the most critical variable because it directly impacts the risk stratification, which the EAU guideline requires assessing. The number of prior biopsies and surveillance status are also crucial as they define the current management context.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
Given the retrieved information—a PI-RADS 4 lesion, a rising PSA trend, and a prior ISUP group 2 diagnosis with prior biopsy history—the evidence supports proceeding with a biopsy to further characterize the lesion, as suggested by the panel.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: biopsy | MISSING: none
